intro: Most kanji words are read by joining the readings of their kanji, but three things break that habit. Some common words have a reading that belongs to the whole word and not to its parts (今日 is きょう). A kanji changes reading depending on whether it stands alone or sits in a compound (山 is やま, 登山 is とざん). And where two parts meet, the sound often changes: a consonant becomes voiced (手紙 てがみ) or doubles into a small っ (学校 がっこう). Learn the whole-word list by heart and learn the two rules for the rest.

skills.rule: These twelve words have a reading that belongs to the whole word: never build it from the kanji.
skills.explain:
今日 きょう, 明日 あした, 昨日 きのう, 大人 おとな, 一人 ひとり, 二人 ふたり, 二十歳 はたち, 上手 じょうず, 下手 へた, 果物 くだもの, 部屋 へや, 時計 とけい. The kanji give the meaning; the reading belongs to the pair as a block. You cannot split きょう into a part for 今 and a part for 日.

Some of these kanji pairs also have a formal on reading, which is a different, stiffer word: 今日 こんにち means 'nowadays' (and survives in こんにちは), 明日 あす or みょうにち and 昨日 さくじつ are for news and business letters. In everyday speech, and in every drill sentence about today, tomorrow or yesterday, use きょう, あした, きのう.

Counting people is irregular only at the start: ひとり, ふたり, then さんにん, よにん, ごにん and so on. Age twenty is はたち; from twenty-one on it is regular (にじゅういっさい).
patterns: 今日 きょう / 明日 あした / 昨日 きのう
一人 ひとり / 二人 ふたり (三人 さんにん onwards is regular)
上手 じょうず / 下手 へた
大人 おとな / 果物 くだもの / 部屋 へや / 時計 とけい

examples.jp: {今日[きょう]}は暑[あつ]いですね。
{明日[あした]}、友達[ともだち]と映画[えいが]を見[み]に行[い]きます。
examples.en: Tomorrow I'm going to see a film with a friend.

examples.jp: 机[つくえ]の上[うえ]に{時計[とけい]}があります。
examples.en: There is a clock on the desk.

examples.jp: 姉[あね]は料理[りょうり]がとても{上手[じょうず]}です。
examples.en: My older sister is very good at cooking.

examples.jp: {大人[おとな]}二枚[にまい]と子供[こども]一枚[いちまい]お願[ねが]いします。
examples.en: Two adults and one child, please.

examples.jp: 弟[おとうと]は来年[らいねん]{二十歳[はたち]}になります。
examples.en: My younger brother turns twenty next year.

contrast.note: A real word, but it means 'these days' in formal writing. 'Today' in a normal sentence is always きょう.
Formal words for 'tomorrow' used in business and news. あす is not wrong in formal text, but the everyday word is あした; みょうにち is never right in casual speech.

contrast.vs: いちにん / さんにん
contrast.note: にん is the regular counter for people, but it starts at three. One and two people are ひとり and ふたり.

mistakes.bad: {今日[こんにち]}は雨[あめ]です。
mistakes.note: Read the whole word: today is きょう, not こん + にち.

mistakes.bad: {一人[いちにん]}で旅行[りょこう]しました。
mistakes.good: {一人[ひとり]}で旅行[りょこう]しました。
mistakes.note: One person is ひとり; にん only starts at three.

mistakes.good: {果物[くだもの]}が好[す]きです。
mistakes.note: Fruit is the native word くだもの, written with these two kanji as a block.

skills.tip: If the word is on the list of twelve, stop reading kanji by kanji and say the whole word you already know: きょう, あした, ひとり, へや.

skills.rule: A kanji standing alone as a word usually takes its kun reading; inside a compound of kanji it usually takes its on reading.
skills.explain:
The kun reading is the native Japanese word: 山 やま, 水 みず, 車 くるま, 花 はな. When the kanji is a word by itself, or carries okurigana (登る のぼる), read it this way. Exception: some single kanji are words only in their on reading: 本 ほん, 駅 えき, 肉 にく, 茶 ちゃ, 絵 え.

The on reading is the borrowed Chinese sound, used when kanji join into a Chinese-style compound: 登山 とざん, 水道 すいどう, 電車 でんしゃ. Most mountain names follow this: 富士山 ふじさん. So 山 in a sentence about walking up a mountain is やま, but the hobby of mountain climbing is とざん.

The exception that matters: some compounds are made of native words and keep kun readings throughout. They are usually concrete, everyday things: 花火 はなび (flower + fire), 手紙 てがみ, 青空 あおぞら, 雨戸 あまど. A few mix the two (本屋 ほんや, 毎朝 まいあさ). When a compound sounds like an old native word, try the kun readings before the on readings.
patterns: kanji alone → kun: 山 やま, 水 みず, 車 くるま, 花 はな
kanji compound → on: 登山 とざん, 水道 すいどう, 電車 でんしゃ
native compound → kun + kun: 花火 はなび

examples.jp: 週末[しゅうまつ]に{山[やま]}へ行[い]きます。
examples.en: I'm going to the mountains at the weekend.

examples.jp: 父[ちち]の趣味[しゅみ]は{登山[とざん]}です。
examples.en: My father's hobby is mountain climbing.

examples.jp: 冷[つめ]たい{水[みず]}をください。
この国[くに]では{水道[すいどう]}の水[みず]が飲[の]めますか。
examples.en: Can you drink tap water in this country?

examples.jp: 毎朝[まいあさ]{電車[でんしゃ]}で会社[かいしゃ]に行[い]きます。
examples.en: I go to the office by train every morning.

examples.jp: 夏[なつ]は川[かわ]で{花火[はなび]}を見[み]ます。
examples.en: In summer we watch fireworks by the river.

contrast.note: さん / ざん appears only in compounds and mountain names (登山, 富士山). The word 'mountain' on its own is やま.
すい lives in compounds (水道, 水曜日). Water to drink is みず.
か is the on reading (花瓶 かびん), but 花火 is a native compound: はな + ひ, voiced to はなび.

mistakes.bad: 冷[つめ]たい{水[すい]}を飲[の]みました。
mistakes.good: 冷[つめ]たい{水[みず]}を飲[の]みました。
mistakes.note: A kanji standing alone as a word takes the kun reading.
しゃ is only for compounds such as 電車 and 自転車; the car itself is くるま.

mistakes.bad: {花火[かか]}を見[み]に行[い]きました。
mistakes.good: {花火[はなび]}を見[み]に行[い]きました。
mistakes.note: 花火 is a native compound read with kun readings, and ひ is voiced to び.

skills.tip: Count the kanji: alone means kun (やま), a compound means on (とざん); watch for native compounds (花火) and on-only words (本, 駅).

skills.rule: In a native compound the second part often voices (て + かみ → てがみ); in an on compound a final つ or ち (before k, s, t, h) or く (before k only) often becomes a small っ (がく + こう → がっこう).
skills.explain:
Voicing (rendaku): when two native words join, the first consonant of the second often becomes voiced: k → g, s → z, t → d, h → b. 手 + 紙 is てがみ, 青 + 空 is あおぞら, 時 + 々 is ときどき, 人々 is ひとびと. It does not happen if the second part already has a voiced sound (一人旅 ひとりたび, not ひとりだび), and words starting with a vowel or m, n, r, y, w cannot voice (色々 いろいろ, 山々 やまやま). Voicing is common but not guaranteed, so learn each word.

Small っ (sokuon): in on compounds, a first kanji ending in つ (and usually ち) doubles before k, s, t or h: 出 + 発 → しゅっぱつ, 雑 + 誌 → ざっし, 一 + 回 → いっかい. A first kanji ending in く doubles only before k: 学 + 校 → がっこう, but 学生 stays がくせい. After っ, h becomes p: 発 + 表 → はっぴょう. Before a vowel nothing changes: 発音 はつおん.
patterns: native + native → voiced: 手紙 てがみ, 青空 あおぞら, 時々 ときどき
on ending つ / ち + k, s, t, h → っ: 雑誌 ざっし, 出発 しゅっぱつ
on ending く + k → っ: 学校 がっこう (学生 がくせい stays)
っ + h → っp: 発表 はっぴょう

examples.jp: 母[はは]に{手紙[てがみ]}を書[か]きました。
examples.en: I wrote a letter to my mother.

examples.jp: {時々[ときどき]}公園[こうえん]を散歩[さんぽ]します。
examples.en: I sometimes take a walk in the park.

examples.jp: 今日[きょう]は{青空[あおぞら]}がきれいですね。
examples.en: The blue sky is beautiful today, isn't it?

examples.jp: 妹[いもうと]は歩[ある]いて{学校[がっこう]}に行[い]きます。
examples.en: My younger sister walks to school.

examples.jp: 明日[あした]、授業[じゅぎょう]で{発表[はっぴょう]}をします。
examples.en: Tomorrow I'm giving a presentation in class.

examples.jp: 飛行機[ひこうき]は九時[くじ]に{出発[しゅっぱつ]}します。

contrast.note: く doubles only before a k sound. Before s it stays: がくせい, but がっこう.
Before a vowel there is no っ and no p: はつおん, but はっぴょう.

contrast.vs: 色々 いろいろ / 山々 やまやま
contrast.note: Repeated words voice only when the sound can voice: ときどき and ひとびと, but いろいろ and やまやま.

mistakes.bad: {手紙[てかみ]}を送[おく]りました。
mistakes.good: {手紙[てがみ]}を送[おく]りました。
mistakes.note: In a native compound the second part voices: かみ → がみ.

mistakes.bad: {学校[がくこう]}は八時[はちじ]からです。
mistakes.good: {学校[がっこう]}は八時[はちじ]からです。
mistakes.note: く before a k sound becomes a small っ.

mistakes.bad: 駅[えき]で{雑誌[ざつし]}を買[か]いました。
mistakes.good: 駅[えき]で{雑誌[ざっし]}を買[か]いました。
mistakes.note: つ before an s sound becomes a small っ.

skills.tip: At the seam, ask: native word? voice it (てがみ). On word: つ or ち before k, s, t, h, or く before k? Double it (がっこう), and h turns to p (はっぴょう).
